text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali says Jordan appreciates Egypt's initiative to mobilise joint Arab market.
- Lawyers sum up defence case today for Jordanian soldier accused of premeditated shooting of Israeli schoolgirls and call for his acquittal.
- Interior Minister Nazir Rasheed says has approved establishment of Jordan's 19th authorised political party, the National Popular Democratic Movement.

- Islamists between the door of boycott and the window of participation. Has the Moslem Brotherhood committed political suicide? Analysts puzzle whether movement has decided to be the great loser in Jordanian politics after its decision to boycott elections. Or is it a tactical move to seek guarantees from the government?
- Government plans to issue temporary law protecting local production, after an anti-monopoly law which is also planned.
- Has the Islamic Action Front lost its raison d'etre after Moslem Brotherhood's call for boycott of elections?
- After Moslem Brotherhood decision to boycott elections and possibility of other opposition parties joining them, is it in Jordan's interest to postpone elections?
- Parliamentary speaker Saed Hayel al-Srour says delaying elections is a constitutional matter but it would be better to hold them on time.
- Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah to visit Qatar on Monday and reaffirm that Jordan will attend Middle East economic conference if invited.
- Bank of Jordan agrees at extraordinary shareholders meeting to raise capital to 21 million dinars.
- Israeli premier to disappoint all unless he changes policy - king.
- Majali to visit three more Arab countries, Saudi Arabia, Yemen and Morocco to discuss means of promoting bilateral relations.
